request.system:
You merge feature candidates extracted from the videos of a Microsoft Business Central launch event into one de-duplicated feature list.
Rules:
- Two candidates are the same feature when they describe the same capability or change, even under different names (e.g. "Copilot chat" and "Microsoft Copilot Chat in Business Central"). A product (the Expense Agent, the MCP server) is not one feature; its individual capabilities are. Keep features at the granularity a developer or consultant would search for.
- Do not invent features, do not drop candidates. Every candidate id appears in exactly one group.
- Use only the candidate texts. No outside product knowledge.
- Names: short, product-like, as the presenters say them, no marketing adjectives. Slugs: lowercase, hyphenated, stable, 2 to 6 words.
- No em-dashes anywhere. Use a plain hyphen.

groups.name: Composite layouts
groups.summary: The old all-in-one report layout is split into a body layout for structure, a theme for look and feel, and a header footer layout. Theme and header footer are applied at runtime, so the same report can be run in different ways.

groups.name: Report themes and header footer layouts
groups.summary: Branding such as colors and fonts, and header and footer content, is defined once as a theme or header footer layout and reused across document reports. The demo shows one customer statement body layout combined with different themes and header footers.

groups.name: Composite layout menu on a body layout
groups.summary: On a body layout in the report layouts page, a composite layout menu lets you pick the theme and header footer for testing. Running the report then shows the chosen combination.

groups.name: Default theme and header footer levels
groups.summary: Default theme and header footer can be set globally, per company, per report and per body layout. Each lower level overrides the one above it.

groups.name: Manage themes and header footer layouts page
groups.summary: From the manage themes and header footer layouts page you can create a new theme or header footer layout with a name and description. You either start blank or upload an existing layout, which then becomes available for use.

groups.name: Themes and header footer layouts from AL
groups.summary: In the rendering section of a report you specify type Word with subtype Theme or Header Footer, while body layouts use subtype Body. Themes use a Word template file.

groups.name: Shipped themes, header footers and body layouts
groups.summary: Microsoft aims to ship themes (calm, default, playful, standard), about eight header footer layouts and around 50 body layouts. Header footers are split into external reports with logo and minimal internal ones, and samples are available for your own report objects.

groups.name: Feature switch for the new document experience
groups.summary: Feature management has a setting to enable or turn off the new document experience. This allows a gradual rollout of composite layouts per environment.

groups.name: Layout status for app-supplied layouts
groups.summary: A Layout status menu on the report layouts page lets an administrator set a lifecycle state such as draft, pending approval, approved or retired on app-supplied layouts, including Microsoft ones. Layouts that are not approved do not show on the request page and only appear on the report layout page.

groups.name: EDI in Business Central
groups.summary: EDI is added to exchange order information between buyer and seller instead of sending email. It is built on the existing E-Documents technology and the PEPPOL format, with a log for each exchange.

groups.name: Purchase order e-document
groups.summary: When the buyer releases a purchase order, an e-document is generated in the background to send to the seller. It carries items, quantities and expected dates.

groups.name: Sales order from inbound e-document
groups.summary: On the seller side, importing the purchase order XML in the inbound e-document list with the PEPPOL format creates a sales order automatically. Dates, items, quantities and amounts are carried over.

groups.name: Order response
groups.summary: The seller can accept or reject the order and send a response back. The buyer imports it and it is linked to the original purchase order e-document with a status.

groups.name: Remittance advice from payment journal
groups.summary: After posting the purchase invoice and applying a payment in the payment journal, the buyer can send a remittance advice file to the seller through the e-document service.

groups.name: E-document types and directions
groups.summary: Four e-document types are covered: purchase order, sales order, order response and remittance advice. Each type can be set to inbound only, outbound only or both.

groups.name: EDI setup
groups.summary: Setup follows the invoicing pattern: e-document setup, vendors and customers set to exchange electronically, and electronic identifiers on both sides. Item reference or GTIN is recommended, and quantities and delivery dates should be filled.

groups.name: E-document linkage from documents
groups.summary: Users can open the created e-document straight from the purchase order via the fact box. Response messages are also visible directly from the document.

groups.name: E-document messages
groups.summary: A message architecture attaches messages such as acknowledgement and order response to the e-document. These messages are linked to the original document.

groups.name: Invoicing for France
groups.summary: Invoicing for France is introduced with three new e-document formats set up on the e-document service, including e-reporting. Lifecycle events such as collected, submitted, accepted, refused and technical rejected are stored as messages linked to the invoice e-document.

groups.name: Override of layout description
groups.summary: For layouts shipped from an app, the developer's description can be overridden by an administrator. The override shows on the report layout page and in the user's view of it.

groups.name: Report inbox APIs
groups.summary: New APIs cover the report inbox operations, where scheduled reports and report packs land. Agents and automation can use them to trigger processing or AI analysis, through Power Platform, an MCP server, Copilot Studio or any API client.

groups.name: API overview page
groups.summary: A new API overview page, shipping in version 29, is the easiest way to find APIs. Searching there shows API names and URLs to try them out.

groups.name: PTE lifecycle management in the admin center
groups.summary: Upload, install and update operations are added to PTE management in the admin center, bringing full PTE lifecycle management into one place. Installs start from the apps page with an install extension button.

groups.name: Deployment schedules for PTE installs
groups.summary: When installing a PTE you can choose immediate, next minor update or next major update, plus a sync mode. Previously in-product installs could only be immediate.

groups.name: App view filter for per tenant extensions
groups.summary: The apps page can be filtered to show different views of installed apps, for example only per tenant extensions.

groups.name: Update a PTE from the admin center
groups.summary: From the app details page you can install a different version of an installed PTE. This triggers an update rather than a new install.

groups.name: Multiple scheduled PTE installs and cancel
groups.summary: Several future installs can be scheduled for the same PTE, for example one version on the next minor and another on the next major update. Scheduled installs show on the app details page and can be canceled before they run.

groups.name: Operations page audit of PTE actions
groups.summary: The environment operations page captures every PTE install, update and scheduling action. Scheduled operations show a target app version and are reconciled to completed when the update starts.

groups.name: Deprecation of in-environment PTE management
groups.summary: PTE management in the extension management pages and in the automation API will be deprecated as of version 30.0. Users should migrate to the admin center within about half a year and not mix both experiences in one environment.

groups.name: Admin center API for PTE operations
groups.summary: Endpoints for all demoed PTE operations are available in the admin center API. S2S apps used by partners do not need in-environment registration and permission sets to upload and install PTEs.

groups.name: Early install of hotfixes for Microsoft apps
groups.summary: Customers can install a prepared hotfix version of a Microsoft app immediately or in the next update window from the app details page. It bypasses safe deployment, so use it only when the version fixes an issue that affects the customer.

groups.name: Dev extensions remain installed on sandboxes
groups.summary: Dev extensions are treated more like PTEs and are not uninstalled during environment updates or other lifecycle operations unless incompatible. This reduces unexpected uninstalls and republishing.

groups.name: Scan receipts with auto capture
groups.summary: From the plus button the user picks scan receipts and the phone's native auto capture grabs receipts automatically. Several receipts can be captured at once and are processed by the Expense Agent.

groups.name: Upload receipts from gallery or files
groups.summary: Existing receipt pictures can be sent to the Expense Agent from the gallery with the operating system share function. The plus menu also offers choose from files.

groups.name: Mileage expenses on mobile
groups.summary: Users create a mileage expense on the phone by entering a destination, choosing a route and picking a vehicle type. Distance and rate are calculated as in the web app.

groups.name: Automatic categorization into expense reports
groups.summary: After upload, the agent recognizes expenses and sorts them into expense reports. In the demo it matched a receipt to an existing report and created new reports for the others.

groups.name: Offline mode
groups.summary: Without a connection users can still add receipts to the app. They are uploaded and processed when the phone is back online.

groups.name: Expense submission and approval on mobile
groups.summary: The mobile app supports submitting expense reports and the full approver experience. Approvers review expenses, check compliance flags, override them and approve.

groups.name: Expense Agent mobile app
groups.summary: A new mobile app for iOS and Android scans receipts, crops the background and works offline. Users accept beta conditions and need a Business Central environment that supports the Expense Agent.

groups.name: Shopify Tax Matching
groups.summary: An AI capability analyzes tax information received with Shopify orders and tries to match it to Business Central tax setup. If no match is found, it creates the missing information.

groups.name: Automatic creation of tax jurisdictions and tax areas
groups.summary: When no match exists, new tax jurisdictions, a tax area and sometimes tax details are created. The demo created a tax area with three new jurisdictions.

groups.name: Tax area code and tax liable on Shopify orders and refunds
groups.summary: Shopify orders get tax area code and tax liable fields, filled from Shopify or by AI and used when the sales document is created, and they can be overridden to skip standard mapping. The Shopify refund page gets a tax fact box and tax lines.

groups.name: Review and approve tax match
groups.summary: A review window shows the tax area, jurisdictions and taxes per shipping and product line. A red icon marks low confidence and the user approves or cancels.

groups.name: US-only TaxMatch extension
groups.summary: The capability is a small US-only Shopify extension not published on AppSource. It is installed by default on new installations based on localization or offered as a prompt on upgrade.

groups.name: TaxMatch fact box and agent settings
groups.summary: A fact box on the Shopify shop card holds settings to activate the TaxMatch agent, allow creating tax jurisdictions and areas, and set a prefix for created tax areas.

groups.name: Tax match review mode setting
groups.summary: Users choose to review matches always, never or only on low confidence. Review cannot be skipped for significant issues such as a missing jurisdiction or different tax rate.

groups.name: AI change notification on sales document
groups.summary: A sales document created from a Shopify order shows a notification that the order was modified by AI. It opens the tax match review.

groups.name: Use Shopify order number
groups.summary: A setting in order synchronization on the Shopify shop card lets sales orders and invoices use the Shopify order number as document number with a Shopify number series. The setting is inherited when an order is imported.

groups.name: Return documents for Shopify refunds and exchanges
groups.summary: Refunds can create a sales return order or credit memo, chosen in the return and refund processing setting, using the same parameters as the sales order. For exchanges, Move Negative Lines creates a sales order or invoice for the exchange line.

groups.name: Tax rate mismatch handling
groups.summary: If the Business Central tax rate differs from the Shopify rate, the order is not created and a review is forced. The user keeps the Business Central rate or overrides it with the Shopify rate.

groups.name: Page scripting generally available
groups.summary: The page scripting tool moves from preview to general availability. It records and replays user actions in the web client, for example for user acceptance tests.

groups.name: Page scripting localization
groups.summary: Every user-facing string in page scripting is translated, including steps, error messages and tooltips. This makes the tool ready for production use in all languages.

groups.name: Page scripting accessibility and usability
groups.summary: An accessibility and usability pass was made on page scripting, with look and feel changes based on feedback.

groups.name: Multiple selection in grids
groups.summary: Recordings can capture selecting several rows in a list and running bulk actions on them. These steps can be replayed.

groups.name: Validate message and error dialog text
groups.summary: A recording can validate the text of a message or error dialog. This turns a recording into a real assertion.

groups.name: Agents generating page scripts
groups.summary: Agents can be used to try to generate page scripts and run them.

groups.name: AL MCP environment symbol search
groups.summary: The AL MCP can search the connected environment and tell which app and version owns each object. The symbol search tool has a source parameter set to environment, so symbols are looked up on the server without downloading them or setting dependencies.

groups.name: Get next object ID tool
groups.summary: An MCP tool reads app.json, works out the ID ranges and suggests free object IDs. In the demo it skipped IDs already in use.

groups.name: AL language server for agents
groups.summary: A standalone AL language server gives project-aware language intelligence over the language server protocol, not tied to Visual Studio Code. Agents resolve definitions, references, types, implementations and callers instead of relying on text search.

groups.name: Default implementation for interface methods
groups.summary: Interface methods can have a default implementation, so implementers do not have to implement newly added methods. Consumers get a warning that a default exists and can still implement their own logic.

groups.name: Required pending attribute
groups.summary: An attribute tells interface consumers that implementing a new method will become mandatory in a later major. Consumers get a warning instead of a break.

groups.name: Public package resources
groups.summary: Resource folders can be marked public so other apps can list and read them as JSON or text by provider app ID, without a dependency. Private resources still work with the normal functions without an app ID.

groups.name: Integer to big integer field change
groups.summary: A field can change from integer to big integer while keeping existing rows, aimed at entries that run out of numbers. The compiler and AppSourceCop warn about implicit conversions and overflow, but the change is allowed without copying data.

groups.name: Keys spanning base and extension fields
groups.summary: Because table extensions are merged into the base table, a key or index can cover both base table and table extension fields. This was a long-requested item.

groups.name: Namespaces in translation IDs
groups.summary: XLIFF files can use fully qualified names including the namespace as ids instead of hash keys. This avoids collisions between same-named objects in different namespaces and makes ids readable.

groups.name: Action inherits page tooltip
groups.summary: An action using RunObject no longer needs its own tooltip, because it comes from the target page. The description is kept in one place.

groups.name: Created by and modified by full name system fields
groups.summary: New system fields hold the created by and modified by full names next to the user ids. They can be placed on pages in code and through personalization or customization.

groups.name: IsDirty on Record and RecordRef
groups.summary: A new IsDirty method on Record and RecordRef tests whether a record has changed. It lets you ask the user to save without comparing fields by hand.

groups.name: Read isolation for isolated storage
groups.summary: Read isolation is an explicit option when reading from isolated storage. You can state read committed with an update lock.

groups.name: Data-driven tests
groups.summary: One test procedure can run against many data sets from a test data source, so more tests come from adding data points. The platform runs the test once for every entry, building the data on demand.

groups.name: Command line test run with JSON output
groups.summary: The whole test suite can be run from the command line. It returns structured JSON with pass, fail and skip counts and a real exit code, so failures fail the build.

groups.name: Test handlers
groups.summary: Test handlers provide setup and tear down in AL, with hooks before and after the test codeunit, test procedure and each data-driven test case. The demo uses a logger handler that traces while tests run.

groups.name: Default test handlers
groups.summary: Regular test handlers are declared by the test codeunit, while default handlers run on every test, including tests from other apps. They suit telemetry setup or running Microsoft test suites against your extension.

groups.name: AL graph
groups.summary: A graph command in the AL tool builds a static call graph across an extension and its dependencies. You or an agent can query who calls whom, external integration points, and public entry points.

groups.name: Profiling MCP for agents
groups.summary: A coding agent can start, monitor and stop a sampling profile through the AL tool proxy or the Business Central MCP server, given a session ID. It returns CPU profile files and an overview of duration, SQL and HTTP calls, and the demo found a background codeunit producing 30,000 rows.

groups.name: Snapshot debugging MCP for agents
groups.summary: Agents can target an environment and start a snapshot recording for the next matching session, capturing values and call stacks. The agent analyzes the results and can place better snap points and re-arm until the cause is found.

groups.name: Project tracking in the Expense Agent
groups.summary: Projects can be used on expenses in the web app. The admin enables project tracking in the setup guide, otherwise the option does not show.

groups.name: Project visibility: all or assigned projects
groups.summary: A setup option decides whether users see all projects or only those they are assigned to. Assigned projects helps with many projects or hidden projects.

groups.name: Assigned resources on the project card
groups.summary: The project card has an Assigned resources section. All assigned resources see that project and its tasks in the web app.

groups.name: Resources on project tasks
groups.summary: Users can be assigned to individual project task lines instead of the whole project. They then pick only their assigned tasks.

groups.name: Resource link on the employee card
groups.summary: Each employee needs a resource selected on the employee card. The system then recognizes the user in expense management.

groups.name: Project and task on a web app expense
groups.summary: In the web app a user selects a project and task on an expense. Only active projects and posting tasks are offered.

groups.name: Project ledger entries from expense reports
groups.summary: The chosen project and task show in the billable information of the expense report. Posting creates project ledger entries automatically.

groups.name: Match production configuration
groups.summary: Administrators can temporarily match a sandbox database configuration to a typical production database. This helps evaluate production behavior, for example for performance work or cloud migration.

groups.name: Restart warning flyout
groups.summary: The admin center button opens a flyout explaining the action and warning that the environment restarts. Connected users are disconnected.

groups.name: Match production operation tracking
groups.summary: The operation can be tracked like other admin center operations. Details show who started it and when.

groups.name: Automatic revert after 72 hours
groups.summary: The environment reverts to a typical sandbox configuration after 72 hours. The revert happens in the first update window after that.

groups.name: Match production usage limit
groups.summary: The operation is limited to three occurrences per tenant per calendar month, each lasting 72 hours.

groups.name: Match production in admin center API
groups.summary: The match production configuration operation is supported in the admin center APIs. Developers can automate it in their processes.

groups.name: Match production paid license requirement
groups.summary: The feature is only available on tenants with a paid license type. This includes partners using the partner sandbox license.

groups.name: Database export reliability
groups.summary: The most common failures were removed across the export pipeline, so fewer than 1% of exports fail. Big environments can be exported reliably.

groups.name: Database export as an environment operation
groups.summary: An export appears on the operations page with status, times, who triggered it and the error on failure. It uses the same filters and details flyout as other operations.

groups.name: Single Export database button
groups.summary: Export database is now one button instead of a dropdown with export history. The flyout notes that progress can be tracked on the operations page.

groups.name: Database export history page retirement
groups.summary: The database export history page is retiring. Its information, plus more, is on the operations page.

groups.name: Export history API endpoint deprecated
groups.summary: The admin center API export history endpoint is deprecated and kept only on API versions 2.29 and earlier. Automations should move to the environment operations API.

groups.name: AI policy compliance check
groups.summary: An admin setting lets AI check expenses against policies configured per expense category, and flag non-compliant or unclear items for the approver. It can use Copilot credits.

groups.name: Presubmission policy check
groups.summary: Submitters can run the AI policy check manually with a check policies button before sending the report. It is not automatic for submitters and can be turned off to save AI credits.

groups.name: Approval history and audit trail in the web app
groups.summary: The web app shows tabs for draft, submitted, approved and history, and approver tabs. History lists each step with timestamps, approver and rejection reason, and tracks amount changes as part of wider approval improvements.

groups.name: Approval history in Business Central
groups.summary: The approval history is shown in the Business Central expense report and posted expense report. Accountants with rights can see it.

groups.name: Interim approvers
groups.summary: An interim approver such as an accountant can check an expense report for compliance. They must approve before the final approver.

groups.name: Approval messaging
groups.summary: Approve and reject actions show different messages, icons and colors.

groups.name: Approval limits
groups.summary: An approver can have a maximum approval amount alongside an unlimited approver. One specific-amount level plus an unlimited level is supported.

groups.name: Ad hoc alternate approver
groups.summary: An approver can delegate pending expense reports to a colleague. All pending reports are redirected.

groups.name: Planned alternate approver
groups.summary: An approver plans an alternate for a date range. Expense reports are redirected automatically in that period.

groups.name: Travel request approval
groups.summary: Approval is added for travel requests. The request shows who approved it and when.

groups.name: Multiple excise taxes per item
groups.summary: The excise fast tab on the item card is replaced by an Excise Taxes page under Related. One item can have several excise taxes.

groups.name: Automatic upgrade of excise configuration
groups.summary: Existing excise configuration from the previous wave is upgraded automatically to the new table and page. No manual action is needed.

groups.name: Bonded location for excise
groups.summary: A location can be marked so excise duty is not calculated on inbound receipt. Duty is calculated when goods leave the bonded location.

groups.name: Transfer entry type in excise permission
groups.summary: Excise permission supports the transfer entry type besides sales, purchase and manufacturing.

groups.name: Ad valorem and hybrid excise calculation
groups.summary: Ad valorem calculates excise as a percent of a taxable amount. Hybrid combines a specific component with an ad valorem component.

groups.name: Self-billing number series per vendor
groups.summary: Each self-billing vendor can have its own number series. Otherwise the Payables setup series is used.

groups.name: Self-billing PEPPOL format
groups.summary: A PEPPOL format is added for self-billing. Self-billing becomes part of the e-documents framework.

groups.name: Cross-environment master data management
groups.summary: Subsidiaries in other environments of the same tenant can pull master data from the HQ company. It is built in, with no middleware or custom code, and uses the same UI as same-environment synchronization.

groups.name: Withholding tax for employees
groups.summary: Withholding tax, previously available for vendors, is extended to employees with new fields for employee rules. Posting an expense report above the threshold creates withholding tax entries, and it can also be used in the general journal.

groups.name: Verifactu in Spain
groups.summary: Verifactu enablement in Spain is generally available. It needs setup, and is on AppSource if uninstalled.

groups.name: Payment times for Australia and Great Britain
groups.summary: Payment times rules are expanded for Australia and Great Britain.

groups.name: Intrastat for Germany and QR invoicing address for Switzerland
groups.summary: New Intrastat reporting in Germany based on Intrastat core. Fully structured address support for QR invoicing in Switzerland.

groups.name: EU BP file export for Germany
groups.summary: EU BP files can be exported with the audit file export in the German localization.

groups.name: SFT in Austria and Iceland
groups.summary: Existing SFT functionality is enabled for the Austria and Iceland localizations.

groups.name: Subcontracting app
groups.summary: The Subcontracting app, released in minor update three, is pre-installed on new environments. It extends the older subcontracting that only registered that the work happened.

groups.name: Installing the Subcontracting app
groups.summary: The app replaces the legacy Subcontracting worksheet, which shows a notification with an install action. Upgraded environments can also install it from Microsoft Marketplace or AppSource in Business Central.

groups.name: Subcontracting assisted setup
groups.summary: An assisted setup fills in default values, lets you change them and links to related pages.

groups.name: Warehouse, price and cost for subcontracting
groups.summary: Subcontracting operations can use standard warehouse processes. More price management and cost allocation are mentioned.

groups.name: Component supply method on BOM lines
groups.summary: A field on production BOM lines sets how a component reaches the subcontractor: transfer, consignment at vendor, or vendor supplied.

groups.name: Subcontracting components on the production order
groups.summary: On a refreshed released production order, subcontracting components get different location codes. Transfer components point to the main location and others to the vendor card location.

groups.name: Components at vendor location field
groups.summary: A vendor card field tracks components still owned by the company at the vendor location. It shows consignment and vendor supplied components.

groups.name: Subcontracting details fact box on routing
groups.summary: A fact box on production order routing shows whether a line is subcontracted, connected components and the WIP quantity at the subcontractor. It drills down to WIP ledger entries and links purchase, transfer and production orders.

groups.name: Create subcontracting order from routing
groups.summary: A subcontracting purchase order can be created from the production order routing with one action. The worksheet remains for bulk operations.

groups.name: Subcontracting purchase order lines
groups.summary: The generated purchase order holds lines for vendor-supplied components, the routing operation, an info line and comment lines with instructions.

groups.name: Subcontracting FastTab in Manufacturing setup
groups.summary: Manufacturing setup gets a Subcontracting FastTab with a Create production order info line toggle. It also holds a component transfer lead time.

groups.name: Subcontracting fact box on purchase lines
groups.summary: A fact box on the purchase line shows the connected production order. It links to production orders, transfer orders, routings and components.

groups.name: Subcontracting comments and attachments
groups.summary: Routing lines get a subcontracting comment copied to the purchase order, editable or inherited from standard tasks. Routing attachments have toggles to flow to the production order and purchase lines, so the supplier gets instructions.

groups.name: Transfer WIP item and WIP ledger entry
groups.summary: A routing line can be marked with a transfer WIP item to track work in progress moved to and from the subcontractor. Posting creates a WIP ledger entry instead of item ledger entries.

groups.name: Create transfer order to subcontractor
groups.summary: A Subcontracting action on the production order creates a transfer order to the subcontractor location. It holds lines for components and the transfer WIP item.

groups.name: Item charges on subcontracting receipts
groups.summary: Item charges can be assigned to posted subcontracting receipt lines, including the operation line. Production order statistics show the charge in subcontractor cost.

groups.name: Subcontractor prices with closest match
groups.summary: Subcontractor prices are matched by closest match on quantity, date, task, unit of measure and variant, not lowest price. A larger order can get a higher unit price.

groups.name: Standard task codes
groups.summary: Standard task codes are included to demonstrate different subcontractor pricing.

groups.name: Minimum amount for subcontractor price
groups.summary: If the line amount is below the vendor minimum, the unit price becomes the minimum amount divided by quantity.

groups.name: Subcontracting with warehouse receipt
groups.summary: For directed put-away locations, a subcontracting order needs a warehouse receipt. Put-away with serial numbers is created only for the last operation, otherwise output is registered.

groups.name: Inventory put-away for subcontracting
groups.summary: Subcontracted items can be received with inventory put-aways on locations requiring put-away and pick. Serial numbers flow into put-away lines and quantity to handle can be auto filled.

groups.name: Serial numbers at any level in subcontracting
groups.summary: Serial numbers can be defined on the production order or the purchase document. Any receiving method works.

groups.name: NST on .NET 10
groups.summary: The Business Central service tier now runs on .NET 10.

groups.name: Streaming Open in Excel
groups.summary: Open in Excel uses a streaming implementation with less memory and fewer out of memory exceptions. Larger files can be loaded.

groups.name: Recent records virtual table
groups.summary: The recent records list is exposed to AL as a queryable virtual table. Records can be deleted, otherwise it is read only.

groups.name: Table extensions stored on base table
groups.summary: Table extension fields are stored on the base table, so no join is needed. Reads are faster and writes up to 30% faster in a benchmark.

groups.name: Index management access
groups.summary: The index management page can be found through Tell Me, including semantic search, and through a Manage indexes button on table information. Indexes, including SIFT indexes, can be disabled there.

groups.name: Enable and disable keys at runtime
groups.summary: A key can be defined with Enabled set to false and enabled by code at runtime. This suits features most customers do not use.

groups.name: System fields in analysis mode
groups.summary: System fields such as created by, created on, modified by and modified on are always available in the analysis mode column picker. This works even if the list page does not show them.

groups.name: System fields in profiles
groups.summary: In the profile page designer, system fields can be found and added to a page. The example adds modified by to the sales order card for all profile users.

groups.name: MCP server landing page
groups.summary: The Business Central MCP server has its own session and a landing page at aka.ms/bcmcp.

groups.name: Reporting features pointer
groups.summary: Reporting has three separate videos and is only pointed to in the server session.

groups.name: Permission overview page in context
groups.summary: The permissions overview page can be opened from the permission sets list, the permission set card and the table information page.

groups.name: Telemetry for Open in Excel
groups.summary: A telemetry signal records who used Open in Excel and when.

groups.name: Microsoft Copilot chat in Business Central
groups.summary: A unified Microsoft Copilot chat opens from the Copilot button in Business Central, replacing the old Copilot UI. It reasons over Business Central data within the user's permissions and context, with progress messages, tables and citations.

groups.name: Web and general knowledge answers
groups.summary: Copilot answers questions not tied to Business Central data using the internet and documentation, such as sales tax setup or travel directions. It can also combine Business Central data with web data, like converting item prices with a web exchange rate.

groups.name: Follow-up conversation and suggestions
groups.summary: Users keep asking in the same conversation and Copilot suggests follow-up questions. Responses are grounded and can include charts and tables.

groups.name: Business Central data questions
groups.summary: Copilot searches Business Central data with the user's context, permissions and company, for example most urgent sales orders. It also analyzes sales data, such as the least sold items, and suggests actions.

groups.name: Work IQ data in Copilot
groups.summary: With the Microsoft Copilot license, Copilot also uses Work IQ data such as calendar, email, Teams and files. The demo finds a customer meeting in the user's calendar.

groups.name: Customer meeting sales brief
groups.summary: Copilot prepares a sales brief from customer data with sales figures, momentum, account risk and talking points.

groups.name: Agentic developer loop
groups.summary: The agent plans an investigation and uses ALSP, the AL tool proxy and the Business Central MCP server for call stacks, variables and CPU profiles. The loop is understand, capture, measure, fix.

groups.name: Connecting to the snapshot debugging MCP server
groups.summary: Connect through the AL tool as MCP host, Visual Studio Code via launch.json starting the snapshot MCP proxy, or your own MCP host.

groups.name: Telemetry-triggered snapshot capture
groups.summary: The agent arms snapshot debugging, sets snap points and polls telemetry for a specific error. When found it downloads the snapshot and reasons about the root cause.

groups.name: Agentic slow SQL analysis via telemetry
groups.summary: An agent watches telemetry for slow SQL calls, finds the session and starts sampling. Its verdict identified an index issue with root causes and fixes.

groups.name: Resolving vague item references
groups.summary: A short query like tell me about S100 is resolved to the matching item by Business Central tools.

groups.name: Page context sent to Copilot
groups.summary: Copilot uses content from the current page, including extension pages, plus knowledge about the user such as role, as hints.

groups.name: Intent detection and agentic loop
groups.summary: Copilot detects intent from the message history and iterates through tools. Tools include Business Central, work data, other agents and the web.

groups.name: Copilot respects user permissions
groups.summary: Copilot runs as the signed-in user and accesses data only within their permissions.

groups.name: Copilot and agent capabilities admin control
groups.summary: The Copilot and agent capabilities page lets admins opt in or out of AI features and control who can use them.

groups.name: Business Central MCP server as data access layer
groups.summary: Copilot gets Business Central data through the same MCP server used for agentic integration. It reaches all tables, including extensions, without custom APIs.

groups.name: Guidance for Copilot-friendly extensions
groups.summary: A Microsoft Learn article gives guidelines for building extensions that Copilot and agents can work with more easily, for example more descriptive ones.

groups.name: Citations, progress messages and sources
groups.summary: Answers include clickable citation pills, progress messages and a sources button listing what the AI used.

groups.name: Feedback on Copilot responses
groups.summary: Users can give thumbs up or down and share screenshots and prompts to help troubleshoot unexpected results.

groups.name: Released production orders from planning worksheet
groups.summary: Carrying out action messages can create production orders as released, or released and print. Flushing posts consumption and capacity on creation.

groups.name: Actionable error on refresh production order
groups.summary: When refresh fails because the routing is not certified, the error explains why and opens the routing.

groups.name: Dynamic previous and next operations in routings
groups.summary: Previous and next operation fields are visible for parallel routings and hidden for serial ones.

groups.name: Machine center calendar entries available until
groups.summary: The machine center card shows until when calendar entries exist, in red when missing. A calculate calendar report is added to the card.

groups.name: Direct transfer modes
groups.summary: Direct transfer can post in one go or create separate shipment and receipt documents. Ship and receipt mode supports partial shipping and warehouse shipment.

groups.name: Direct transfer mode and transit location on transfer routes
groups.summary: Transfer routes have fields for direct transfer mode and transit location. Defaults come from inventory posting setup and can be overridden.

groups.name: No blank-location inventory posting setup
groups.summary: Inventory posting setup entries with empty location are no longer needed. Transit locations are used and location code is always filled on manufacturing value entries.

groups.name: Inventory pick for direct transfers
groups.summary: Outbound and inbound transfers can be posted together from an inventory pick, including partial quantities.

groups.name: Failed quality inspection blocks transfer
groups.summary: Posting a transfer is blocked for a tracked item with a failed inspection, and the error opens the inspection.

groups.name: Quality inspection assignment and role-based control
groups.summary: Changing a header field prompts self-assignment. Quality admin or supervisor roles can change quantities, reassign, reopen or delete finished inspections.

groups.name: Automatic passed and failed quantity
groups.summary: Finishing an inspection moves the sample size to passed or failed quantity, usable in workflows.

groups.name: Side-by-side data view
groups.summary: Data Copilot finds can be opened side by side with the chat while the conversation continues.

groups.name: EUDR fields on the item card
groups.summary: The item card Sustainability tab gets EUDR relevant and EUDR commodity fields. Item tracking is needed for these items.

groups.name: EUDR certificate capture
groups.summary: A tab on the Lot No. Information card holds certificate number, schema, dates, DDS information and country for EUDR items. It can also be used for other schemas such as FSC.

groups.name: EUDR flag on purchase lines
groups.summary: Purchase orders and receipts get a line-level EUDR flag.

groups.name: Certification details on sales invoice
groups.summary: The sales invoice layout can print the lot, certification schema and certification number.

groups.name: Order traceability by EUDR batch
groups.summary: With item tracking you can see which orders used batches with EUDR information.

groups.name: Updated data picker
groups.summary: The Word add-in data picker got UX improvements. It shows the company information data set next to report information.

groups.name: Company information data set
groups.summary: A company information data set is always shipped with Word layouts, so authors need not add it themselves. It is useful for header and footer layouts.

groups.name: Table builder editing
groups.summary: The table builder can edit an existing table definition through the wizard, not only insert tables.

groups.name: Address design control
groups.summary: A design block offers three address formats, such as sender, receiver and shipping address in three columns.

groups.name: Field group design control
groups.summary: A design block for label and value pairs as a column grid, single or double stacked. It will be used in new body layouts.

groups.name: Amounts design control
groups.summary: A design block that shows calculations with captions and values. It does not calculate anything.

groups.name: Signature line design control
groups.summary: A signature line block with two types and custom captions. It is used in quality management.

groups.name: Notes design control
groups.summary: The notes control asks how many bullet points you want and adds the component.

groups.name: Hide if control
groups.summary: A content control hides or shows its content based on a chosen boolean value.

groups.name: Boolean expressions for Hide if
groups.summary: Later you will set a boolean expression on data set values to hide or show content. A small formula language will be part of it.

groups.name: Sample layouts for themes
groups.summary: The Word add-in has sample documents to preview style, font and color changes. You then save, clear the content and upload as a theme.

groups.name: Header and footer authoring help
groups.summary: A new header footer layout comes with the company information data set. In Word you add default header or footer versions, modify and upload them.

groups.name: Tariff code sync
groups.summary: Tariff number and country from the item card are sent to Shopify as HS code and country of origin. A shop card toggle controls import and export.

groups.name: Find mapping by barcode toggle
groups.summary: A hidden field controls fallback to barcode search when SKU mapping fails. Disabling it avoids duplicate variant links but requires manual mapping.

groups.name: Unlisted product status
groups.summary: The connector supports Shopify's unlisted status, sold by direct link but hidden in the store.

groups.name: Skipped record notification in price sync
groups.summary: Foreground price sync shows a notification when records are skipped, for example sales blocked items.

groups.name: Skipped records and API errors in the role center
groups.summary: The Shopify activities part shows counts of skipped records and API errors across stores.

groups.name: Provide feedback button
groups.summary: A provide feedback button lets users report problems with details and files to the Microsoft team only.

groups.name: B2B company synchronization by default
groups.summary: B2B company synchronization is visible by default. Adding a company creates the company, a customer and a catalog on Shopify.

groups.name: Auto create B2B catalog
groups.summary: The toggle creates a catalog linked to the company location so Business Central prices apply. Market catalogs are an alternative for simpler plans.

groups.name: B2B catalog import and duplicates
groups.summary: B2B catalogs are imported only when the company exists in Business Central. Price sync is prevented for catalogs linked to two company locations.

groups.name: Company tax registration ID and country extensions
groups.summary: Tax registration IDs are now populated when creating customers. Small Belgium and US extensions are added, and Belgium adds an Enterprise number option.

groups.name: Contact numbers on Shopify orders
groups.summary: Sell-to, bill-to and ship-to contact numbers can be shown on Shopify orders. They are filled automatically and can be changed.

groups.name: Bookmark views to role center
groups.summary: A bookmark view action on analysis views and saved list views puts the view on the role center. It suits views used as mini reports.

groups.name: Bookmarks in profiles
groups.summary: Bookmarked views can be added to a profile's role center for all its users.

groups.name: Mileage rates per period
groups.summary: Mileage allowance can have start and end dates for several periods. The rate is picked based on the expense date.

groups.name: Mileage rates per vehicle type
groups.summary: Mileage rates can be set per vehicle type from a new table, combined with periods. The user picks the vehicle type on the mileage expense.

groups.name: Standard mileage rate
groups.summary: The standard rate setup still works. If filled, the new rate setup is not used.

groups.name: Automatic mileage amount calculation
groups.summary: The amount is filled from the date and vehicle type when creating a mileage expense.

groups.name: Currency code on mileage rates
groups.summary: Mileage rates have an optional currency code field.

groups.name: Test data source interface
groups.summary: An interface with one function to list test cases and one to build test context objects. Sources can be resource files, generated cases, tables or web services.

groups.name: Strongly typed test context
groups.summary: The data source returns an ITestContext, but the test can use its own interface for typed test data.

groups.name: Data-driven tests in Test Explorer
groups.summary: After one run, all test cases appear in the VS Code Test Explorer. Running selections and debugging work as usual.

groups.name: Data-driven tests via AL tool and AL MCP
groups.summary: Data-driven tests can also run through the AL tool and the AL MCP.

groups.name: AI Test Toolkit migration to data-driven tests
groups.summary: AI Test Toolkit data-driven tests do not use the new system yet and cannot run from VS Code. Migration is planned.

groups.name: Test handler registration via enum extensions
groups.summary: Handlers are registered by extending the test handler enum for opt-in or the default test handler enum for global.

groups.name: ITestHandler interface
groups.summary: The interface offers before and after hooks at codeunit, procedure and test case level. All have default implementations.

groups.name: TestHandlers property
groups.summary: A test codeunit property takes a comma-separated list of handlers. A codeunit can implement the interface and register itself.

groups.name: Migration from test toolkit events to test handlers
groups.summary: Test handlers are separate from the test toolkit events. Users of those events must migrate to get the new functionality.

groups.name: Skipping test cases with test handlers
groups.summary: Handlers can skip test cases, for example AI tests once a monthly token limit is exceeded.

groups.name: AL graph meta model extraction
groups.summary: An extract subcommand builds a JSON meta model of caller-callee relationships once. Later queries run against it.

groups.name: AL graph query language
groups.summary: A query language supports complex queries such as all callers of an object or methods touching a table. It is documented on MS Learn.

groups.name: DGML and SARIF export
groups.summary: Results export as DGML for humans or SARIF for agents.

groups.name: HTTP client caller query
groups.summary: A query exports everything calling the HTTP client, excluding tests, as a call path tree.

groups.name: Non-debuggable boundary audit
groups.summary: A query finds debuggable callees of non-debuggable methods, where a breakpoint could leak content.

groups.name: Mirroring to Microsoft Fabric
groups.summary: Business Central data is synchronized live into OneLake through an open mirroring database. Setup is three steps: mirror database, connect, choose tables and companies.

groups.name: Fabric connection setup
groups.summary: A Fabric integration app holds the workspace and mirroring database setup. Connect to Fabric builds the infrastructure and test connection checks write access.

groups.name: Table and company selection for Fabric
groups.summary: You choose which tables and companies to synchronize, then start synchronization.

groups.name: Configuration packages for Fabric tables
groups.summary: Configuration packages define tables to synchronize, for example for the Power BI apps. ISVs can ship their own package.

groups.name: Mirrored data with SQL endpoint
groups.summary: Tables are stored as Delta Parquet files in the mirroring database. The SQL endpoint allows normal SQL queries.

groups.name: Power BI apps on Fabric
groups.summary: The Power BI apps were converted to the Fabric backend. They will come as samples or on AppSource in single- and multi-company versions.

groups.name: Multi-company Power BI reporting
groups.summary: Multi-company app versions show data across companies with a company filter.

groups.name: Synchronization overview and details logs
groups.summary: Overview and details logs are under monitoring with views for all, errors or pushed data.

groups.name: Fabric integration APIs
groups.summary: Setup and monitoring data are available as six APIs listed on the API overview page.

groups.name: Export logs pushed to Fabric
groups.summary: Synchronization logs are also written into Fabric for monitoring through the SQL endpoint.

groups.name: Permission sets for Fabric integration
groups.summary: Permission sets cover activation, administration and read-only configuration access.

groups.name: Withholding posting groups on employee and expense category
groups.summary: The withholding business posting group goes on the employee card and the product posting group on the expense category.

groups.name: Withholding tax group
groups.summary: A category can use a tax group holding several product posting groups with a component order for calculation.

groups.name: Gross, net or gross up calculation base
groups.summary: The calculation base can be gross, net or gross up.

groups.name: Simple or compound withholding calculation
groups.summary: With several taxes you choose simple or compound calculation.

groups.name: Withholding thresholds
groups.summary: Thresholds can be per line, document, category per period or total in period, with month, quarter, year or fiscal periods.

groups.name: Withholding at invoice or payment
groups.summary: Withholding is calculated on expense report posting or on payment, staying unrealized until paid.

groups.name: Withholding tax on expense report posting
groups.summary: An expense above the threshold produces a withholding tax entry on posting, visible in preview posting.

groups.name: Employee withholding exemption and certificate
groups.summary: A posting group can mark an employee exempt. Optional certificate number and type fields exist.

groups.name: Pull-based incremental synchronization
groups.summary: HQ stays read-only and subsidiaries pull only the changes across environments.

groups.name: Entra app registration and consent
groups.summary: An Entra app with API read/write all permissions is registered and the HQ admin gives consent in Business Central.

groups.name: Permission set for HQ read access
groups.summary: A purpose-designed permission set with read access to default tables is assigned to the app user in the source.

groups.name: Pictures and attachments sync
groups.summary: Pictures and attachments travel with the synchronized record.

groups.name: Cross-environment setup wizard
groups.summary: A wizard collects privacy consent, the HQ environment and company, and the app client ID and secret, stored securely.

groups.name: Shared or per-subsidiary app registration
groups.summary: One app can be shared across subsidiaries or one registered per subsidiary, depending on audit needs.

groups.name: Initial cross-environment synchronization
groups.summary: Start all runs default tables in a predefined order, starting with business relations and dimensions.

groups.name: Change propagation and synchronization log
groups.summary: Source changes show in the subsidiary after about a minute. Logs and job rescheduling work as for single-environment sync.

groups.name: Subcontracting app replaces Italian subcontracting
groups.summary: Italian subcontracting is discontinued and replaced by the global Subcontracting app. One key difference is around work in progress items.

groups.name: Legacy subcontracting toggle
groups.summary: An Italy-only Manufacturing Setup field indicates legacy subcontracting. It is off on new environments and on for upgraded ones.

groups.name: Legacy subcontracting pre-check
groups.summary: An action checks for open transfer and purchase orders with WIP items before disabling legacy subcontracting. The same checks run on disable.

groups.name: Install Subcontracting app from Manufacturing Setup
groups.summary: The app can be installed from Manufacturing Setup when disabling legacy subcontracting. Without legacy data no migration runs.

groups.name: Italian Subcontracting Migration app
groups.summary: A separate app, not on AppSource, migrates legacy Italian data and is proposed only when needed. It now works in production environments.

groups.name: Run migration by disabling legacy subcontracting
groups.summary: Disable legacy subcontracting runs the migration, restarts the session and switches application areas. Activation is blocked while unmigrated data exists.

groups.name: Subcontracting views on purchase and transfer orders
groups.summary: Legacy subcontracting pages are gone and migrated documents appear in normal lists with a subcontracting view.

groups.name: Migrated vendor fields and subcontracting prices
groups.summary: Vendor subcontracting fields are migrated and the work center link stays. Prices move to the new table.

groups.name: BC-Bench evaluation framework
groups.summary: A reproducible open-source framework evaluates AI coding agents on real AL tasks from real PRs and tests. It measures the impact of model, tool, instruction and agent changes.

groups.name: BC-Bench bug fixing category
groups.summary: Agents fix bugs in the real codebase across 101 tasks from bugs human engineers fixed.

groups.name: AL MCP server for coding agents
groups.summary: The AL MCP server exposes compile, publish and search to agents without VS Code. It improved pass@5 by almost 10% in BC-Bench at the cost of longer runs.

groups.name: Agent harness comparison
groups.summary: With the same model, GitHub Copilot CLI and Claude Code showed no significant difference. Model choice matters more.

groups.name: Contamination detection
groups.summary: Models get only the repo name and bug description and must name files to modify. Only one task matched across 101 tasks and three models.

groups.name: BC-Bench code review category
groups.summary: A category tests whether AI can review AL changes against an expected comment. An LLM judge scores whether generated comments match.

groups.name: AL code review approaches
groups.summary: BC-Bench compares plain Copilot CLI, BC Quality as a plug-in and the AL review agent. The review agent focuses on security, privacy and performance and already comments on BC apps PRs.

groups.name: Run BC-Bench on your own data set
groups.summary: Partners can fork the open-source repo and use their own bug fixes, tests and PRs. Contamination should be checked for open-source repos.

groups.name: Free-text expense policies per category
groups.summary: Policies are free-text lines linked to expense categories, including custom ones. Each policy should be its own line.

groups.name: Flagged and compliant policy statuses
groups.summary: Reports and lines show compliant or flagged, with AI reasoning beside flagged expenses. Missing receipt info also flags a line.

groups.name: Receipt itemization
groups.summary: More receipt itemization is planned so AI can evaluate policies such as alcohol in a meal.

groups.name: Policies pending after changes
groups.summary: Changing merchant or description resets the status to policies pending until re-evaluated.

groups.name: Submit with policies pending
groups.summary: Submitters can submit with pending policies. The system evaluates them and routes to the approver.

groups.name: Approver override of policy flags
groups.summary: Policies are guidance and approvers can still approve flagged expenses.

groups.name: Mandatory override reason
groups.summary: Approvers will need a reason to override a policy, kept in audit records.

groups.name: Policy check availability rules
groups.summary: The check is unavailable without policies or when the report is unchanged since the last evaluation.

groups.name: Uncategorized accounts views
groups.summary: Two saved views on the chart of accounts show accounts without category or subcategory. This helps explain missing financial report data.

groups.name: Where-used for G/L accounts in financial reports
groups.summary: Where-used on the account card shows which financial report definitions use the account.

groups.name: Totaling fact box on row definitions
groups.summary: A fact box on row definition lines shows the G/L accounts in the totaling filter, with navigation.

groups.name: Totaling fact box on column definitions
groups.summary: The same G/L accounts fact box is on column definitions with totaling.

groups.name: Test preview for row and column definitions
groups.summary: A default counterpart definition can be set for testing, and a test button shows the full report.

groups.name: Line type defaulting in definitions
groups.summary: New lines in row or column definitions default to the type of the previous lines.

groups.name: Report packs
groups.summary: A package defines a list of reports with filters and dates. Running it gives one PDF.

groups.name: Scheduling report packs
groups.summary: Report packs can be scheduled and land in the report inbox.

groups.name: Change log for financial report definitions
groups.summary: Change log is set up automatically on financial report definition tables, auditing changes with user ID.

groups.name: MCP data tools
groups.summary: Four system tools (find tables, table relations, table schema, data query) let an LLM write AL queries that Business Central compiles and runs, with no APIs needed. Compiler errors return to the agent so it can correct itself.

groups.name: Server features box in MCP configuration
groups.summary: The MCP configuration page separates server features from APIs and shows which system tools each feature enables.

groups.name: MCP server on/off toggle
groups.summary: A toggle on the Copilot and agent capabilities page activates or deactivates the MCP server as a whole.

groups.name: Travel requests
groups.summary: Employees request permission to spend with budget, dates and justification, and the company sees expected expenses. On approval an expense report per trip follows and receipts are assigned to it.

groups.name: Travel request lines with currency
groups.summary: Requests can be itemized with foreign amounts translated to local currency, plus schedule and locations.

groups.name: Travel request reference on expense report
groups.summary: The expense report specifies its travel request and shows actuals.

groups.name: Audit link between G/L entries and travel request
groups.summary: Posted G/L entries link to the travel request so auditors see who authorized the spend.

groups.name: Foreign currency budgeting
groups.summary: A request can be budgeted in foreign currency and an action updates the local amount at travel time.

groups.name: Travelers on a travel request
groups.summary: A list of other travelers can be added to the request.

groups.name: Automatic expense report from travel request
groups.summary: Requests made in the Expense Agent create the expense report automatically. In Business Central it is created manually.

groups.name: Travel requests in web and phone app
groups.summary: Travel requests will come to the web and phone apps but were not ready at recording.

groups.name: Sustainability formulas on purchase documents
groups.summary: Formulas from journals can be used on purchase orders and invoices, with recalculation on change.

groups.name: Finding sustainability entries
groups.summary: Sustainability entries can be found like other entries.

groups.name: Value chain emissions in more documents
groups.summary: Value chain emissions are available in item, item reclassification and FA reclassification journals and service management.

groups.name: Scope 3 tracking by item tracking
groups.summary: The item card sets average or specific method so lots or serials carry their own emissions.

groups.name: ESG report per lot
groups.summary: The ESG report layout can print information per lot.

groups.name: Reverse sustainability ledger entries
groups.summary: A reverse button works like for G/L entries, for multiple entries, with reversed and reversed-by columns.

groups.name: Collect Amount from GL remembers posted amounts
groups.summary: Collect amount from GL suggests only the part not yet posted.

groups.name: Emissions on fixed assets
groups.summary: FA journals show sustainability account and CO2, and reclassification splits emissions by a CO2 percentage.

groups.name: Refreshed Expense Agent web app
groups.summary: The web app has a refreshed user experience.

groups.name: New languages for Expense Agent
groups.summary: Czech, Dutch, Icelandic, Italian, Norwegian and Swedish will be added to the five current languages.

groups.name: Expense Agent worldwide availability
groups.summary: Expense Agent will roll out gradually to all countries starting in October.

groups.name: Credit card statement upload
groups.summary: Uploaded statements are processed and kept as credit card feed records.

groups.name: Credit card reconciliation with expenses
groups.summary: Card records are matched to existing expenses or create new expenses awaiting receipts.

groups.name: VAT reclaim on expense reports
groups.summary: VAT details from receipts build a VAT specification per line, with multiple rates. Posting uses normal VAT posting groups and creates GL and VAT entries for accountant review.
